slides.title: The Medical Plan Defined
bullets: The central strategic document for a product or therapeutic area
The medical equivalent of a business plan for Commercial
States what to achieve, with whom, through what activities, with what indicators
Spans an annual cycle within a multi-year, product-lifecycle vision

slides.title: Three Phases of Medical Planning
bullets: Situation analysis: disease landscape, competitive position, stakeholder insights
Medical strategy: a clear vision, strategic objectives, and key drivers
Tactical plan: prioritized initiatives with owners, timelines, success criteria

slides.title: A Plan Fed by the Whole System
bullets: Draws on evidence gap analysis, KOL mapping, field insights, congress intelligence
Those inputs come from earlier modules of this course
It feeds and coordinates the evidence, publication, education, and congress plans
Those component plans are covered later in this same module

slides.title: Medical Plan vs Commercial Plan
bullets: Commercial is organized around sales volume and market share
The Medical Plan is organized around scientific objectives and medical value
Closing evidence gaps, building quality relationships, rigorous evidence generation
This distinction justifies Medical Affairs' independence and non-promotional nature

slides.title: Connecting Daily Work to Global Strategy
bullets: Understand the full architecture, not just the tactical part you execute
Connects your daily activity to the product's global strategy
Lets you explain the purpose behind every visit, insight, and collaboration

takeaway.title: The Medical Plan turns medical strategy into an executable, measurable plan
bullets: It mirrors a business plan but is built around medical value, not sales
Situation analysis, strategy definition, and tactical planning are its three phases
It connects to every other component plan covered in this module
